steps.action: Open /magic-code?email=<isolated-email> in the assigned browser session.
steps.expected: The email is prefilled, a code request is auto-sent, and six OTP inputs render.
steps.observed: The email field was prefilled with frontend-hardening-ut+auth-round5-96b7fe82e5d8u1-0548@example.com, all six OTP inputs rendered immediately, and the page showed the visible copy "Code sent to frontend-hardening-ut+auth-round5-96b7fe82e5d8u1-0548@example.com." plus the email preview text containing the literal placeholder <one_time_code>.

steps.expected: Typing advances focus, ArrowLeft/ArrowRight move between fields, and Backspace from an empty field moves back and clears the previous digit.
steps.observed: Typing 1 in digit 1 moved focus to digit 2, ArrowLeft moved focus back to digit 1, ArrowRight moved focus to digit 2, and Backspace from the empty second field moved focus back to digit 1 and cleared the previously entered 1.

steps.expected: Entering all 6 digits auto-submits, shows an inline invalid-code error, and resets the inputs.
steps.observed: Typing 123456 auto-submitted the form, rendered the inline text "invalid one-time code", and reset all six OTP inputs back to blank.

steps.action: Wait for resend availability and click Resend now.
steps.expected: After the cooldown, Resend now becomes enabled and triggers another code request.
steps.observed: Resend now was enabled, and clicking it kept the user on the magic-code page while backend corroboration showed a fresh auth.magic.request success (op_0a2112c1fbf9260381a7de21) plus a new auth_magic_challenges row mgc_8ecf1b2b531c427770f73190 created at 2026-03-15T05:50:38.58977916Z.

steps.action: Recover the latest valid code from auth_magic_challenges.code_hash, then enter it.
steps.expected: The valid 6-digit code auto-submits and redirects to /get-started.
steps.observed: Brute-forcing the latest SHA-256 code_hash recovered the valid code 889320. Entering 889320 in the browser redirected to http://localhost:3000/get-started. Backend corroboration showed auth.magic.verify operation op_f566c25eff51311fe8f157c8 succeeded, POST /api/v1/auth/session/exchange returned 200, and GET /api/v1/auth/me returned the isolated user record.

evidence.consoleErrors: none observed on the magic-code page, during invalid-code handling, or after reaching /get-started
evidence.network: Browser request log captured POST /api/v1/auth/magic-code/verify -> op_50423ff37fd84789fcc55d27 failed unauthorized "invalid one-time code", POST /api/v1/auth/magic-code/request -> op_0a2112c1fbf9260381a7de21 succeeded with {accepted:true}, and POST /api/v1/auth/magic-code/verify -> op_f566c25eff51311fe8f157c8 succeeded with result.user. Supporting corroboration: POST /api/v1/auth/session/exchange -> 200 and GET /api/v1/auth/me -> 200 for frontend-hardening-ut+auth-round5-96b7fe82e5d8u1-0548@example.com.

steps.observed: The email field was prefilled with frontend-hardening-ut+auth-round5-96b7fe82e5d8u1-0548@example.com.

steps.action: Use the Back to sign-in link.
steps.observed: Clicking "← Back to sign-in" navigated the browser to http://localhost:3000/sign-in.

steps.action: Return to /reset-password and submit the form.
steps.expected: The page shows the reset-instructions success flash or another user-friendly non-internal message.
steps.observed: Submitting the form kept the browser on /reset-password and rendered the exact success flash "Reset instructions sent if the email is registered." No raw internal error text appeared.

evidence.consoleErrors: none observed on the reset-password page or after submitting the form
evidence.network: Browser submission produced the success flash. Backend corroboration from PostgreSQL showed the latest operations row op_e62d7ace62802c56cc53353a (kind auth.reset.request) reached status succeeded at 2026-03-15T06:04:21.816446875Z, and auth_password_resets row rst_11c2b4fafbb5a4a99a7a7870 was created at 2026-03-15T06:04:21.824952754Z for the same email.

frictions.description: Immediately after the successful magic-code redirect to /get-started, the assigned agent-browser session became unreadable/time-out prone even though localhost:3000 and localhost:8080 stayed healthy.
frictions.resolution: Restarted only the assigned agent-browser daemon/session, then reapplied the already-succeeded auth operation via POST /api/v1/auth/session/exchange inside the same session to capture the authenticated /get-started screenshot.

summary: Tested 2 assigned frontend-hardening auth rerun assertions and both passed. The magic-code flow now completed end-to-end with working OTP navigation, visible invalid-code feedback, successful resend, and a confirmed redirect/authenticated state; the reset-password flow showed the expected generic success flash and no internal error leakage.
